key_insight: DrugHarness is an evolvable agent framework that helps AI systems perform computational drug discovery more reliably by combining many scientific tools with the ability to learn and adapt from prior execution outcomes. It can improve over time by inducing new skills from trajectories and feedback.
problem_solved: Computational drug discovery requires agents that can coordinate many scientific operations, use biomedical resources, and adapt to changing evidence and constraints. Existing setups often struggle to preserve context across steps and to evolve skills as tasks become more complex.
method: Builds an agent harness with over 80 scientific operations, biomedical resources, and task-specific code in one environment.
Preserves links between candidates, results, and generated artifacts so the agent can track scientific context across the workflow.
Learns from execution trajectories and outcome feedback to induce new conditional skills and adapt behavior over time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, DrugHarness offers a practical blueprint for building more capable scientific agents that can handle long-horizon, tool-heavy workflows. It is especially relevant for domains where reasoning, execution, and adaptation must work together under real-world constraints.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing candidate generation, tool execution, feedback, and skill induction
Icon grid representing the 80+ scientific operations and biomedical resources
Workflow loop illustrating how trajectories feed back into evolving agent skills
Entity-link graph showing relationships among candidates, results, and artifacts
paper_title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
paper_authors: Yuxing Chen, Zhisheng Zhang, Cheng Tang, Wei Li, Minghui Zhang
